 Buying deep out-of-the-money (OTM) puts on QQQ is a high-risk, asymmetric bearish strategy. You risk a relatively small premium for potentially substantial returns if the Nasdaq-100 drops sharply. However, these options have low probabilities of finishing in the money and can expire worthless. Timing is everything: a market decline may not be enough if it happens too slowly, because time decay (theta) erodes option value. Implied volatility also matters; puts can become expensive when fear is already elevated. Consider buying puts before identifiable catalysts, choosing sufficient time to expiry, and sizing positions so total premium loss is manageable.
